editorial.headline: Hand Tool Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25931 covers the making of hand tools and related tool equipment, with national PMA access at 100% but a Bali PMA block under the recorded moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25931 is the industrial code for making hand tools: the practical, durable implements used in workshops, farms, building sites, repair benches, and small production floors. The record names carpentry hand tools such as pliers and screwdrivers; agricultural hand tools such as hoes, shovels, sickles, egrek, dodos, and axes; and equipment for hand tools whether powered or not, including drill bits, hammers, and grinding knives. It also reaches into the making of press tools, mould boxes and moulds, crimping tools, and blacksmith tools such as forging tools and anvils.

That scope makes this a manufacturing activity rather than a trading, retail, or repair category. The centre of gravity is fabrication: turning metal, tool components, and workshop processes into finished or supporting tools. It is broad enough to cover both familiar manual implements and more specialised tool-making equipment, but it remains anchored in what the slim record actually lists. For a founder, the useful reading is simple: this code is for producing the tools themselves, not merely selling them or using them as part of another service.

On scale, the record is unusually clean. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That means the classification is not presented as a narrow large-industry lane only, nor as a protected micro activity only. A small workshop making agricultural hand tools and a larger manufacturer producing press tools or drill-bit equipment both sit within the same recorded scale range, provided the activity being registered matches the manufacturing scope above. The code therefore has a wide operational envelope, but that should not be confused with automatic permission in every location or ownership structure.

The national-versus-Bali picture is the real decision point. Nationally, the record marks KBLI 25931 as TERBUKA for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain terms, the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. Bali is different. The record says the activity is blocked for PMA registration in Bali: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” It also records the moratorium rule as: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).” So the honest reading is this: KBLI 25931 is nationally foreign-open, but a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side record supplied here.
